exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong map work reads coordinates like an architect — here is how one student designed a zoo map.

traits.sample: The lion habitat sits at (−4, 3): 4 left of center, 3 up — I always say x first, then y.
traits.why: The pair is interpreted in words, proving the student reads the plane.

traits.sample: The aviary at (−4, 3) and the café at (5, 3) share a y, so the distance is |−4| + |5| = 9 units across.
traits.why: Absolute value is the tool, and the same-coordinate condition is stated.

traits.sample: My scale is 1 unit = 50 meters, so the 9-unit path is 450 meters — about a 6-minute walk.
traits.why: The scale converts map math into real distances a visitor would feel.

traits.sample: The mirror-image garden is the fountain reflected over the y-axis: (6, 2) becomes (−6, 2) — only the x flips.
traits.why: It states exactly which coordinate changes and why.
